research_question: Analyze the spatial distribution of the orchid Vanilla karenchristianae and its synonyms in Brazil to evaluate the significance of a newly discovered population in the Atlantic Forest.

phase_1.user_prompt: I am documenting a new population of the orchid Vanilla karenchristianae in the Brazilian Atlantic Forest. To understand how significant this range extension is, I need to find all previous occurrence records of this species in Brazil. Since its taxonomy has been updated recently, I should also include its synonyms Vanilla uncinata and Vanilla ensifolia in my search.

phase_2.user_prompt: Download the occurrence records for these three orchid species in Brazil. Please ensure the data includes coordinate information so I can map their spatial distribution.

phase_3.user_prompt: Process the downloaded records to identify valid occurrences. Clean the data to remove records without valid coordinates. Additionally, a previous study noted that specimens from the state of Amazonas identified as these taxa are actually misidentifications of a different species (V. labellopapillata), so please filter out any records located in the state of Amazonas. Count the total number of remaining valid occurrence records.

phase_4.user_prompt: My new field observation is located in Candeias, Bahia, at coordinates 12°36'36''S, 38°29'02''W. Calculate the shortest distance over the Earth's surface between two latitude/longitude points (in kilometers) between this new observation and the nearest previously known occurrence from the cleaned GBIF data. Finally, generate a map showing the spatial distribution of the GBIF records alongside this new point, and save it as `vanilla_range_extension_map.png`.

checkpoint.reference_conclusion: The new record in Bahia represents a significant eastern range extension into the Atlantic Forest, located approximately 2380 km away from the nearest previously known locality (which was in the Amazon).
checkpoint.visual_description: A map of Brazil showing previous occurrence points (e.g., in Pará/Rondônia) and a new, distinct occurrence point far to the east in Bahia near the coast.
